fact: ITWeb says the UNDP puts biometric enrolment at roughly 1.5 million people in a population of around 20 million, about 7.5% (6.8% of the 21.9 million held).
The World Bank appraisal says INRIS has registered 15 percent of adults using biometrics, a coverage gap of about 85 percent (an adults share, so below a third of the whole population).
UNDP says INRIS has enrolled 1.5 million people with biometrics; against the 21.9 million population held here that is about 6.8% (the source gives no population share and says 9 million adults).
